subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO checklist — FintechCo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO checklist — FintechCo

Hi Chris / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Per our ask during the call, attaching a short SLO checklist so we can align on performance targets and next steps for a short POC/load test. Quick recap of the items we discussed and what we need from your side: 

- Latency targets: what p50/p95/p99 do you consider acceptable for the user-facing flow?
- Throughput: expected sustained req/s and peak TPS during business hours
- Concurrency: expected simultaneous users hitting the inference path (both average and peak)
- Streaming: do you require token-by-token streaming for the UI / playback? If yes, is chunked HTTP streaming sufficient or do you prefer a websocket/gRPC stream?
- Sample payloads: a few representative prompts + typical input lengths (avg/99th percentile tokens)
- Success criteria: decision criteria you’ll use after the POC (latency p95 below X, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy fallback tolerance, etc.)

Attached: fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx (fillable) and redwood-latency-benchmarks.pdf (representative numbers from similar customers).

Can you reply with the items above filled in, or a short note with the targets so we can scope the Dedicated pool and proposed test plan? Once we have that, I’ll loop in Aditya (infrastructure) to size the POC and propose dates.

Thanks,

— Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the attachments. See our initial answers below (happy to iterate):

- Latency targets: p50 ~ 80–120ms, p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms (for short replies ~ <40 tokens). For longer completions ( >200 tokens) we expect streaming; end-to-end perceived latency should be < 800ms to first token and streaming thereafter.
- Throughput: baseline 200 req/s across US region, burst up to 600 req/s during peak windows.
- Concurrency: active concurrent sessions typically 30–50; synchronous inference concurrency for webhook-style calls expected to peak around 300 true simultaneous model requests during trading spikes.
- Streaming: yes — token-by-token streaming is required for conversational UI. We prefer HTTP chunked streaming to start (browser compatibility), but can evaluate gRPC streaming later.
- Sample payloads: attaching two example prompt files (short-chat.json, long-gen.json) — typical input length avg 18 tokens, 99th percentile 420 tokens.
- Decision criteria: p95 latency <=250ms for short replies, streaming first token <=800ms, end-to-end throughput at 200req/s with <=5% error rate, and cost target TBD (finance will weigh-in).

Two asks from our side before PoC:
1) Preliminary slot estimate + cost for a 2-week Dedicated POC (predictable throughput)
2) An outline of the load test plan and what data/artifacts you’ll need from us (sample payloads, API keys, monitoring hooks)

Thanks — Chris

Hi all — quick pre-read while I build the detailed estimate. Based on the targets: p95 <=250ms for short responses, streaming first token <=800ms, baseline 200req/s, burst 600req/s — here are rough constraints and what we’ll validate during PoC:

- Model variant: recommend a quantized Llama-2 13B family variant with optimized kernels for NVidia H100 (or equivalent); we’ll provide two flavors: lower-cost int8 and a higher-accuracy int4 quantized profile.
- Concurrency & batching: to hit p95 250ms under 200req/s we’ll rely on small continuous batching with low-latency kernels and prefix KV caching for conversational flows. We estimate ~8–12 GPUs in Dedicated pool for baseline 200req/s with autoscale headroom to hit bursts, subject to final token-distribution.
- Streaming: HTTP chunked streaming supported out-of-the-box; we’ll provide frontend snippets and a Node/Fetch example.
- Load-test plan: we’ll run incremental ramp tests (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%, 300% of baseline) capturing p50/p95/p99, first-byte-to-client, token throughput, token per-second per GPU, and error/retry rates.

What we need from FintechCo to finalize:
1) Representative payloads (short-chat.json + long-gen.json) — please drop in the Drive link or reply to this thread.
2) Expected tokenization rules (any custom stop sequences or special truncation rules).
3) Preferred region for the Dedicated pool (US-West or US-East).

I’ll follow up with a spreadsheet with the GPU counts and estimated monthly/2-week POC cost figures. For the immediate POC, we can provision a time-limited Dedicated pool for the 2-week run; procurement paperwork is the only blocker.

— Aditya
